votes.motion: Approve the minutes of March 3rd as submitted

budget_items.what_was_said: The chair and Joe met with the town manager to double-check the warrant numbers and carefully word an added explanation of how PACC's funding is derived, given town residents who object to any tax money supporting the committee.
Joe reported the committee's current balance, noting January and February interest had been added but March interest and a February Comcast payment had not yet posted.
Joe restated the balance and said an additional amount plus March interest still needed to be added once posted; he needed to follow up with Mileen on a report to track it.
Joe reported the station is currently producing the majority of its content locally and is looking at additional downloadable programs from other stations to add to the total.
The budget is described as essentially finalized after going through select board-type review ("pin kong"), with only minor adjustments remaining before town meeting.
A presentation on new studio space was made to the select board; the committee is unsure where the funding for it will come from and expects to learn more at town meeting.
No report was available this month; it was due from Mileen on the first Monday of the month and the chair asked Joe to follow up.

decisions.decision: Pre-production on the new show 'New England Knits' is on indefinite hold at the host's request.
Talk of the Town is being revamped into a segmented show, and the town moderator is being asked to host it instead of the town manager to avoid a conflict of interest.
Recording of the revamped Talk of the Town is expected to begin in June, pending the moderator's decision to join.
The Eagle House donated furniture (chairs, rocking chair, small table) to the studio at no cost, prompting a redesign of the storytime set.
Storytime is set for Wednesday the 16th; the start time (proposed 11 o'clock) may need to change to accommodate the host's schedule.
The chair asked Joe to encourage Mileen to send the enterprise fund investment report.

minutes.headline: PACC carefully reworded its town-meeting warrant article amid concern no tax money should fund cable access.
minutes.summary: The Public Access Cable Committee held a short, mostly administrative meeting: it approved the March 3rd minutes, reviewed the wording of its town-meeting warrant article with the town manager to avoid public backlash over taxpayer funding, and heard the manager's monthly report covering a completed welcome video, a stalled new knitting show, a revamped Talk of the Town format, donated studio furniture, and an unresolved cable-fee/interest balance. No substantive votes were taken beyond approving minutes and adjourning.

what_happened.line: The committee reworded its town-meeting warrant article with the town manager to address resident concern that no tax money fund cable access.
It approved its March 3rd minutes without discussion.
Pre-production on a new knitting show is on indefinite hold at the host's request.
Talk of the Town is being redesigned as a segmented show, with the town moderator asked to host instead of the town manager to avoid a conflict of interest.
A presentation on new studio space went to the select board, and the committee said it does not yet know where that funding would come from.

why_it_matters: The warrant article's wording is what residents will read and vote on at town meeting, and it turns on whether cable access draws on tax dollars or a separate fee.
Studio space funding remains unresolved, so any cost would need to surface at town meeting before residents are asked to approve it.
